subsystems.name: Micro-bot unit
subsystems.role: the individual agent — a centimetre-scale or smaller device that senses, moves, computes and radios.

subsystems.name: Local mesh layer
subsystems.role: lets nearby units find each other and pass messages hop by hop.

subsystems.name: Consensus and coordination layer
subsystems.role: turns thousands of local decisions into one coherent collective behaviour.

subsystems.name: Localisation and timing
subsystems.role: every unit needs to know roughly where and 'when' it is without a global fix.

subsystems.name: Aggregation backbone
subsystems.role: bridges local swarms to the wider world.

subsystems.name: Fabrication and power supply
subsystems.role: making and fuelling units by the billion.

buildSteps.title: Define the collective task
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the swarm as a whole must achieve and what each unit must therefore sense, carry and do — this fixes size, power and cost per unit.

buildSteps.title: Design the unit
buildSteps.detail: Balance actuator, radio, processor and power budget so a single device weighs a few grams at most and costs cents to make.

buildSteps.title: Fab the units
buildSteps.detail: Use semiconductor-style batch processes for sensors and logic, then pick-and-place assembly for actuators and power, so millions come off a line.

buildSteps.title: Build the radio and mesh stack
buildSteps.detail: Engineer neighbour discovery, hop-by-hop routing and spectrum sharing that still work when node density is extreme.

buildSteps.title: Write the swarm algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Design purely local rules — follow neighbours, vote, claim a task — then prove emergent global behaviour in simulation with very large agent counts.

buildSteps.title: Validate in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Run hundreds to a few thousand physical units in an arena, with tracking cameras providing ground truth, and close the gap between sim and reality.

buildSteps.title: Scale production
buildSteps.detail: Reach billion-unit output; a planetary swarm implies trillions, which needs manufacturing and materials flows far beyond today's robotics industry.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and interconnect
buildSteps.detail: Start with contained swarms in one site, then link gateways into regional then global networks.

buildSteps.title: Engineer control and safety
buildSteps.detail: Add authentication, kill switches, containment zones and rollback so a planetary-scale collective can always be shut down.

prerequisites.why: flying and walking micro-robots have been built in labs, but only in small numbers and short runs.
multi-hop radio networks are well understood and deployed, though not at trillions of nodes.
protocols for agreeing across many unreliable nodes exist; their behaviour at planetary scale is untested.
a millimetre-to-centimetre device cannot carry enough fuel or battery for long unattended operation.
ranging and inertial methods work indoors or underwater but drift; a planetary swarm has no single positioning service.
no industry today produces robots, or even simple electronic nodes, at that volume and cost.

pathway.milestone: lab swarms of tens to a few thousand simple robots
pathway.unlocks: demonstrations that local rules produce collective behaviour such as clustering and shape formation.

pathway.milestone: field swarms of thousands to millions for monitoring, agriculture or inspection
pathway.unlocks: real autonomous operation outdoors over weeks, with reliable mesh links and battery swap or harvesting.

pathway.milestone: standards for inter-operating swarms and gateways
pathway.unlocks: independent swarms from different makers joining one network.

pathway.milestone: regional collectives of billions of units
pathway.unlocks: sensing and acting at landscape scale, if energy, manufacturing and control problems are solved.

pathway.milestone: planet-wide mesh of trillions of units
pathway.unlocks: a single coordinated organism-like system — the tile's premise, and currently unproven at every layer.
